exercises.title: Issues 1 — what kind of requirements issue?
exercises.problemHtml:
Early in a project nearly all logged issues relate to requirements: requests for clarification, scope decisions, feasibility questions and to-do items on the requirements. Categorising them helps route each to the right owner and spot patterns (many feasibility questions may signal over-ambitious requirements).

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Các loại vấn đề yêu cầu thường gặp.

Yêu cầu

  • Trả lời mọi câu trong khung trả lời rồi bấm Nộp.
  • Đúng hết mới được Accepted; giải thích từng câu hiện sau khi nộp.

exercises.title: Issues 2 — development or management effort?
exercises.problemHtml:
Track the effort spent on requirements. Requirements development effort: planning requirements activities, workshops and interviews, analysis, writing, reviews, prototypes. Requirements management effort: configuring an RM tool, submitting and evaluating changes, updating the repository, communicating changes, tracking and reporting status, creating trace information.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: Issues 3 — read an iteration burndown
exercises.problemHtml:
A burndown chart shows the story points remaining in the backlog after each iteration — which, unlike "percent done", also reveals scope growth. Write function forecastEnd(remaining): given the points remaining after each completed iteration (e.g. [120, 100, 85, 60], the first value is the starting backlog), compute the average burn per iteration over all completed iterations and return how many more iterations are needed to reach zero (rounded up); return Infinity if the average burn is 0 or negative (scope is growing as fast as work is done). Also set SCOPE_GREW to true if any iteration ended with more points than the previous one, for the sample BURNDOWN.

Requirements

  • forecastEnd([120, 100, 85, 60]) = 3 (average burn 20 per iteration).
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Viết forecastEnd(remaining): tốc độ "đốt" trung bình mỗi vòng, số vòng CÒN cần (làm tròn lên), Infinity nếu không giảm; và SCOPE_GREW cho dữ liệu mẫu.

Yêu cầu

  • forecastEnd([120, 100, 85, 60]) = 3 (trung bình 20 điểm/vòng).
hintsJson: Tốc độ trung bình = (đầu − cuối) ÷ số vòng đã xong.
Số vòng còn = ceil(còn lại ÷ tốc độ).

exercises.title: Issues 4 — managing requirements on agile projects
exercises.problemHtml:
Agile accommodates change through iterations and a dynamic product backlog: new stories that arrive mid-iteration are prioritised against the remaining backlog and allocated to future iterations; the team always works on the highest-priority stories.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Agile đón thay đổi qua backlog động: story mới giữa vòng được xếp ưu tiên và đưa vào các vòng sau.

Yêu cầu

  • Trả lời mọi câu trong khung trả lời rồi bấm Nộp.
  • Đúng hết mới được Accepted; giải thích từng câu hiện sau khi nộp.
